editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-category writeup (590 words, within the 400-1200 range) with a standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Claims are attributed sentence-by-sentence to the specific outlet that reported them, and every body URL is present in article.sources (no orphan-source gap).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 source snapshots in full from sources/2026-09/google-launches-pics-an-ai-image-creation-and-editing-app-built-into-workspace/ (source-0.html.gz = workspace.google.com official blog post, source-1.html.gz = TechCrunch (Sarah Perez, Sep 1 2026), source-2.html.gz = 9to5Google (Abner Li, Sep 1 2026)). Verified sha256 of each decompressed file matches manifest.json. All three fetched at status_code 200 with suspicious_patterns: null. Cross-checked every claim: (1) Nano Banana attribution to TechCrunch/9to5Google confirmed verbatim in both ('powered by Google's Nano Banana image-generation model' / 'Leveraging Nano Banana, Google Pics offers "precise, object-based image editing."'); Google's own blog post never names the model, matching the article's 'What We Don't Know' claim. (2) pics.new access flow, import sources, and the six editing features (object select/edit, text edit/reformat/translate, crop, 2K/4K upscale, batch edit+revert) all verbatim/near-verbatim in the Google blog's bulleted list. (3) TechCrunch's 'collaborative editing' and 'several different generations... pick the best one' claim confirmed. (4) Docs/Slides integration and future Drive integration ('coming weeks') confirmed in all three sources. (5) The exact quoted fragment 'prompt to create' is verbatim in the TechCrunch snapshot ('Google Pics is a tool where you prompt to create, not where you design something new from scratch'); no other text is presented as a direct quote. (6) Tier list (Business Standard/Plus, Enterprise Standard/Plus, Google AI Pro/Ultra, Google AI Pro for Education) matches both Google's blog and 9to5Google exactly. (7) 9to5Google's I/O 2026 announcement / Sept 1 GA date matches its byline dateline and text ('Following the announcement at I/O 2026 in May, Google Pics is launching in general availability today', dated Sep 1 2026). No hallucinated quotes, no misattributions found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No unsupported claims found. One minor cross-source tension the article doesn't surface: TechCrunch describes the rollout as happening 'over the coming weeks' for 'most Workspace customers,' while Google's own blog and 9to5Google frame it as available 'starting today' / GA reached. This is an immaterial hedge in one outlet's phrasing, not a factual conflict the article got wrong — Google's primary-source blog (the most authoritative of the three) is unambiguous that GA started same-day, and the article follows that. Not significant enough to require a correction.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. No promotional language, no unsourced editorializing; the Analysis section frames Pics relative to Canva/Adobe Express using only claims already attributed to TechCrunch.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ and grepped 2026-06 through 2026-08 for 'Google Pics', 'Nano Banana', and 'Google Workspace' — no existing article covers this launch or topic.
